'''Haywood Christopher Owens''' (born March 1, 1979) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played briefly in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Standing at {{height|ft=6|in=8}}, he played the [[power forward]] position.

==College career==
Owens played one year at [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane University]]<ref>{{cite news |author1=J. Douglas Foster |title=Top stars in unison for game - Owens, Sasser lead North squad |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98154733/tip-stars-in-unison-for-game-owens-sa/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |date=28 July 1997 |page=37|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> before moving at [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|The University of Texas at Austin]],<ref>{{cite news |author1=Mark Rosner |title=Mystery solved: Owens will be a force in debut season |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98153948/mystery-solved-owens-will-be-a-force-in/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |date=5 December 1999 |page=C15|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> where he graduated in 2002.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110430193448/http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/hist-chris-owens.html Chris Owens at Texas Longhorns.]</ref> On December 29, 2001, he suffered a season ending knee injury in a loss against Utah.<ref>{{cite news |author1=Jim Vertuno |title=Bad timing - Horns limp into Big 12 season with Owens out |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98154371/bad-timing-horns-limp-into-big-12-seas/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[The Monitor (Texas)|The Monitor]] |date=5 January 2002 |page=4B|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author1=Mike Jones |title=Horns facing new test of will |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98154544/horns-facing-new-test-of-will/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |date=4 January 2002 |page=10D|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref>

==Professional career==
[[File:Chris Owens defending against Dmytro Zabirchenko.jpg|250px|thumbnail|right|Owens at the Ukrainian All-Star game in 2011]]
Owens was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in the 2nd round of the [[2002 NBA draft]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/draft2002/board/index.html |title=NBA Draft Board |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 29, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309164213/http://www.nba.com/draft2002/board/index.html |archive-date=March 9, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> but he was then traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. He played in one [[NBA]] game with the Grizzlies.

Owens' first and only NBA game was played on April 15, 2003, in a 86 - 97 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]] where he recorded 4 points and 1 rebound.

He then played in the [[United States Basketball League]] with the Cedar Rapids River Raiders. He arrived in [[Europe]] in 2004, signing with Banca Nuova Trapani, with whom he played 30 games, averaging 19.1 points and 9.1 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.legaduebasket.it/player/?id=OWE-CHR-79 |title=Chris Owens at Legaduebasket.it |access-date=March 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722041926/http://www.legaduebasket.it/player/?id=OWE-CHR-79 |archive-date=July 22, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2005, he moved to [[CB Granada]] of the [[ACB League]], but he was released in January 2006.<ref>{{cite news|title=Granada splits with Chris Owens|url=http://www.hoopbets.com/news/Spain/334/18012006/Granada_splits_with_Chris_Owens.html|accessdate=July 21, 2013|newspaper=Hoopbets.com|date=January 18, 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304091229/http://www.hoopbets.com/news/Spain/334/18012006/Granada_splits_with_Chris_Owens.html|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He spent the rest of the season in the [[Continental Basketball Association]] with the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] and in the [[Greek Basket League]] with [[Panionios BC|Panionios]].

For the 2006–07 season he signed with [[ALBA Berlin]] of Germany.<ref name="espn" /> The following year, he moved to [[Galatasaray Café Crown|Galatasaray]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Galatasaray signs Chris Owens|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/15693/3735/galatasaray-signs-chris-owens|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130721023120/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/15693/3735/galatasaray-signs-chris-owens|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 21, 2013|accessdate=July 21, 2013|newspaper=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=October 1, 2007}}</ref>

In 2008, he moved to [[BC Donetsk]] in Ukraine. He stayed there until February 2010, when he signed with [[Panellinios BC|Panellinios]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Panellinios tabs Haywood Chris Owens|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/cups/eurocup/5844/panellinios-tabs-haywood-chris-owens.html|accessdate=July 21, 2013|newspaper=Sportando.net|date=February 18, 2010}}</ref>

In September 2010. Owens signed with [[BCM Gravelines|Gravelines]] in France,<ref>{{cite news|title=Gravelines Dunkerque land Haywood Owens|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/France/basketball.aspx?NewsID=202416|accessdate=December 17, 2014|newspaper=Eurobasket.com|date=September 5, 2010}}</ref> but he played only 4 games in the [[LNB Pro A|French League]].<ref>[http://www.lnb.fr/fr/Pro-A/200006/Joueurs/A21122/Owens-Chris?saison=2010 Chris Owens at French League.]</ref> In November 2010, he returned to Ukraine and signed with [[BC Azovmash|Azovmash]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=AZOVMASH tabs veteran Owens|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2010-11/i/77692/4674/azovmash-tabs-veteran-owens|accessdate=July 21, 2013|newspaper=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=November 1, 2010|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20130721023121/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/home/transactions/eurocup-2010-11/i/77692/4674/azovmash-tabs-veteran-owens|archivedate=July 21, 2013}}</ref>

For the 2011–12 season he signed with [[KK Cedevita]] of Croatia.<ref>{{cite news|title=KK Cedevita lands Chris Owens|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/adriatic-league/29123/kk-cedevita-lands-chris-owens.html|accessdate=July 21, 2013|newspaper=Sportando.net|date=July 4, 2011}}</ref> In July 2013, he signed a one-year deal with [[KTP-Basket]] of Finland.<ref>{{cite web|title=Haywood Owens next to Finland|url=http://basketball.eurobasket.com/Finland/news/326362|publisher=Eurobasket.com|accessdate=August 17, 2013}}</ref>

In September 2014, he signed with [[Argentino de Junín]] of Argentina.<ref>[http://www.diariojunin.com/noticias/42306_haywood-chris-owens-es-el-nuevo-extranjero-de-argentino-.html Haywood Chris Owens es el nuevo extranjero de Argentino]</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the great-nephew of 1930s [[African American|African-American]] [[track and field]] star, [[Jesse Owens]],<ref name=espn>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2537189 Jesse Owens's great-nephew to play in Berlin.]</ref> who won four gold medals at the [[1936 Summer Olympics|1936 Berlin Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news |author1=David Hancock |title=An Owens Returns To Berlin |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/an-owens-returns-to-berlin/ |access-date=22 March 2022 |work=[[CBC News]] |date=30 August 2006}}</ref>
